newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan churches urge speedy constitutional reforms.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan churches urge speedy constitutional reforms.

text.p: Kenya's churches paid for a two-page advertisement in all three Nairobi Sunday newspapers to call for constitutional reforms ahead of elections due later this year.

The Kenya Episcopal Conference, which links Catholic churches in the country, and the National Council of Churches representing most Protestant churches, proposed countrywide Ecumenical prayers to back their appeal.

The advertisements appeared despite condemnation from President Daniel arap Moi, who last week said the churches' call, announced at a press conference in Nairobi, amounted to an ultimatum and was dictatorial.
In the advertisements, the churches said they have been advocating broad-based reforms for 10 years but a promise of a major constitutional review by President Moi in 1995 has not been honoured.

They went on to call for better separation of the powers of the executive, judiciary and legislature. They condemned detention without trial and the use of laws to restrict movements, ban meetings, remove diplomatic privileges and censor the media.
"We appeal to the government to make urgent arrangements so as to facilitate these reforms before the next general elections," the churches said.
